This is the cycle of the moon, which is 28 days in length.
There is also a 29 day and 30 day version of a lunar cycle. The 29 days are called the New Moon cycle, and the 30 days the Full Moon. Both are 28 or 29-day cycles. In this article, we will focus on the 28- day lunar month.
How does the lunar calendar work?
 the calendar is divided into 28 (or 29) days. Every day is named by the day of it's respective month, for example:
The 28th day would be called Moon Day. Moon Days are divided by 28, so that every 3 Moon days is 2, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 and 36 days, respectively. When you add up all the Moon day divisions, you get the number of days to a month (Moon days = 1 + Moon months = 28). The moon phase cycle is 1 day, or 28 Moon cycles per year. Each lunar year is approximately 29.53 days long, as a whole. (There are exceptions to this, such as the year of 2012, when the full moon was on December 21st and has been a full month since then.)
 and from the Wikipedia article on lunar cycles:
 The lunar day length is defined as 365.2425 days (± 0.017). This is called a "leap year" because it occurs on average every four years, except in leap years. This calendar has 365 days per cycle or lunar phase. There are 365 lunar months in each cycle (30 days) and 28 lunar days of each month are used to count the days from a new moon to the next new Moon (i.e. the first, second and third days). When a year has exactly 28 months, the month named next in the list of months is considered the new month as of that date. Note that this means that the 29th month is not considered a leap month because there is no next month to be added to it. So the leap year occurs in every cycle when a calendar year ends in March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December, etc. As mentioned above, there are three different versions of lunar phases. Cocoa beans are made in large quantities from sugar and then ground into a powder called cocoa solids. Once the cocoa is ground, there are two distinct steps: the first step is to heat the ground chocolate to around 200°F (93°C) and the second step involves a process called extrusion. The extruder is the machine that turns the raw cocoa into chocolate bars. When you buy a bar of milk chocolate, for example, the chocolate bar is pretty much made as you would expect it to be. There's not much extruded cocoa. Instead, a small amount of raw chocolate goes through the extruding machine and is heated to the desired temperature. This is why milk chocolates have more cocoa and semi-sweet choccies have less cocoa (see below). The process of extruting the milk and making chocolate has to take place in order for the bars to have the right texture, color, and taste. To extrude the choco-coated bars, two types of machines are used: one uses a hand crank to turn the crank and grind the cacao beans, while the other uses an automated machine called a homogenizer. A homogenous chocolate machine will grind all of your cocoa together, leaving you with a smooth, uniform bar. Because the process is automated, most chocolate makers use this machine to make their bars because it's cheaper than an actual hand-cranked machine.
How do you know if your chocolate contains cocoa? text:
The tourbillon is the most famous and most beautiful of the mechanical watches, and it was invented by Augustin Jourdan. It was his attempt to combine the elegance of a tour-bronze watch and the accuracy of an automatic movement. In his own words, "I wanted to create a watch that was both a beautiful and a precise instrument of time".
 a photo of August Journan's tourbanon I was curious about the first watch made with the new tourbon, so I went to see August's workshop. The tourbalon was a very complex watch, weighing around 80 kg.
It had a polished steel case with a large, gold-plated, tourbellows and an all-metal winding stem. There were also two additional pieces, the balance wheel and crown. All the components were hand-finished by a master watchmaker. An entire year was spent making the watch. August also created a bracelet for the movement, which was made from black leather, with gold and platinum links. This bracelet was quite a success, since it came with one of many interesting complications. On the back of this bracelet were engraved the words "Tourbun" and "Règle de Chronographe", the latter meaning "master of chronograph". The watch had an inner, transparent, dial. But it had no visible seconds hand, nor was it possible to read the hour and minute hands. So the second hand was moved by the crown, by means of spring bars, just like the seconds of any automatic watch of that time. A winding mechanism and chronometer certification were added to the label on the inside of its case. That's the way that August created his tourbaillon, a masterpiece that is still in production today. I think that he was very satisfied with it, because it made the timepiece so easy to wear, while still being very beautiful. Although it is a big watch – it has a diameter of about 48 cm – the winding system is very small and precise. If you have a second watch in your hand while wearing it – as I often do – you will notice that it always goes to zero, even when you pull the hand back.
